questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official US Open results or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the 2026 tournament. The champion ranks above the runner-up, followed by semifinalists, quarterfinalists, and earlier-round finishers. Resolve once no remaining match can change the identity of the uniquely highest-finishing U.S. player. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of June 22, 2026 ATP rankings, Ben Shelton (World No. 5, Stuttgart champion, 2023 US Open semifinalist) and Taylor Fritz (World No. 7, 2024 US Open finalist, Stuttgart/Halle finalist) are near co-favorites to be the deepest-advancing American man in New York. Two-time US Open semifinalist Frances Tiafoe (World No. 19, fresh off winning Halle ATP 500 over Fritz), Queen's Club finalist Tommy Paul, and fast-rising 20-year-old World No. 18 Learner Tien form the next tier, with the top five capturing 93% and leaving 7% for Sebastian Korda, Alex Michelsen, and other US entrants.

questions.title: Who will receive the longest prison sentence at the trial over the July 2023 burglary of Gianluigi Donnarumma's Paris home?
questions.background: Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his partner were attacked during a burglary at their Paris home in July 2023.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Paris Criminal Court's judgment, as documented by the court or reliable contemporaneous reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the defendant receiving the longest total prison sentence in the trial verdict delivered by September 30, 2026. Compare sentences actually imposed, including any suspended portions, rather than sentences requested by prosecutors. Later appeals do not affect resolution. Accepted Answer Format : The defendant's name as publicly reported.
questions.current_reasoning: In May 2026, a Paris examining magistrate ordered three adult defendants to stand trial before the Paris Criminal Court (tribunal correctionnel) over the July 2023 Donnarumma home-jacking (two minors go separately to juvenile court, and a sixth suspect died in prison). Ilyas Kherbouch ('Ganito', 21) is overwhelmingly favored to receive the longest sentence: prosecutors allege he was the principal mastermind from Villepinte prison, he already received 7 years in Dec 2024 for the Simone Zanoni home-jacking (triggering statutory recidivism), escaped prison for 13 days in March 2026, and is the sole defendant publicly named in full. Co-mastermind Khyan M. ('Kiki', 21) carries ~18-20% risk of the top sentence if Kherbouch's denial partially succeeds, split between reporting as 'Khyan M.' (10%) and his currently unpublished full surname or the anonymized third adult defendant.

questions.title: Which country will Washington propose as a possible venue for renewed trilateral Russia–Ukraine ceasefire talks by September 25, 2026?
questions.background: The United States has been involved in efforts to broker an end to the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country publicly identified by Ukraine's president as Washington's proposed location for renewed talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, using the proposal current as of September 25, 2026. A suggested location is sufficient; the talks need not have taken place. Resolution Date : 2026-09-25 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: U.S.-brokered trilateral Russia–Ukraine talks paused after the February 16, 2026 Geneva round when the U.S.–Iran conflict began; in March, Washington proposed holding talks in the United States (Miami/Washington) while Russia refused and proposed Turkey or Switzerland, and an earlier Abu Dhabi round was shelved. As of June 24, talks remain frozen though U.S.-Iran diplomacy shows early signs of easing. If Washington proposes a venue for renewed trilateral talks by September 25, Turkey (24%) and Switzerland (22%) are the strongest compromise venues acceptable to both Kyiv and Moscow, while the United States (18%, Washington's standing proposal), the United Arab Emirates (14%, previously scheduled host), and Saudi Arabia (9%, 2025 talks host) remain key alternatives.

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country had publicly acknowledged deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit as of June 2026, though counterspace competition has accelerated sharply around the U.S. Golden Dome program, Russian co-orbital/alleged nuclear ASAT testing, Chinese LEO 'dogfighting' satellites, and France's YODA/TOUTATIS patrol-satellite programs. Conditional on a qualifying official acknowledgment in 2026, the United States (42%) is most likely due to its Space Force orbital warfare posture (Mission Delta 9), active deterrence declassification debates, and major mid-September defense/space forums (AFA Air, Space & Cyber). Russia (28%) is second given its unmatched co-orbital projectile tests and Kremlin willingness to announce strategic weapons for deterrence, ahead of China (14%, traditionally adhering to 'peaceful space' rhetoric), France (9%, openly pursuing laser-armed bodyguard satellites), and India (4%).

questions.title: Which stadium will UEFA select to host the 2029 men's Champions League final?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official announcement awarding hosting rights for the 2029 men's Champions League final, or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution Date : Resolve when UEFA publicly announces its venue selection. Subsequent venue changes will not alter the answer. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the selected stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: UEFA's June 10, 2026 final dossier deadline closed with a strict two-horse race between Barcelona's Camp Nou and London's Wembley Stadium, to be decided by the UEFA Executive Committee in Thessaloniki on September 14-15, 2026. Camp Nou holds a slight edge: its 104,600-seat renovation with ~9,000 VIP seats offers record UEFA revenue, marks 30 years since its 1999 final, serves as a 2030 World Cup rehearsal amid thawed Barça-UEFA ties, and Wembley already hosted the 2024 UCL final plus the July 2028 Euro final just 11 months earlier. Wembley remains a formidable 44% contender because Madrid's Metropolitano hosts the 2027 UCL final and Camp Nou carries residual renovation risk.
